title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether adding a deterministic network verifier to an LLM-driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM-alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026-A1-prereg-v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt-5-mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM-alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with a single automated repair iteration). Primary estimand (executed): paired success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) the guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894, respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥0.20) was not observed. A prespecified sensitivity analysis treating failed episodes as regressions yields paired difference = 0.015 (3/200) with unchanged McNemar discordant counts (p = 0.25). We reconcile an earlier wording inconsistency in the preregistration (regression‑rate vs success‑rate phrasing) by documenting that the executed estimand was the paired success‑rate difference (numerically equivalent to the negative regression‑rate difference). We release the full evidence bundle (execution manifest, raw outputs, verifier traces, analysis artifacts and hashes) and discuss ceiling effects, verifier coverage, missingness, and inference limits.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for intent→configuration translation in NetOps. Practical adoption requires operational reliability: LLM proposals must avoid functional regressions and unsafe intermediate states. Generate→validate→repair architectures—where a deterministic verifier checks proposals and allows guided repair—are a promising safety pattern, but quantitative, preregistered evidence measuring verifier impact in a within‑task paired design is scarce. We therefore ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM-driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and blast radius versus an LLM-alone pipeline on a seeded synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired confirmatory design (CNSM2026-A1-prereg-v1; prereg SHA256 feba320e...eba3); (2) a deterministic, Dockerized execution/analysis pipeline (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) exercising gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 across 200 stratified tasks; (3) a complete, artifact-backed confirmatory analysis and transparent resolution of a preregistration wording inconsistency (regression‑rate vs success‑rate), plus preregistered sensitivity reporting.
sections.related_work: This work intersects (a) LLM-driven network configuration and repair benchmarks and pipelines (Cornetto-like task generation, intent‑to‑config translation) and (b) verifier/guardrail and tool-interactive LLM correction architectures (CRITIC-style critiques, verifier-augmented agents, MeshAgent-like translation+verification). Prior studies compare models or propose architectures; our study isolates verifier impact in a preregistered paired estimator and publishes full execution artifacts for reproducibility.
sections.methodology: Preregistration & estimand: The study preregistered ID CNSM2026-A1-prereg-v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) before observing outcomes. The executed primary estimand (and the quantity used for confirmatory inference) is the paired success‑rate difference: P(success|guarded) − P(success|baseline). Note: the preregistration text also phrased the primary hypothesis in regression‑rate terms; regression_rate_difference = − success_rate_difference. For transparency we adopt the executed estimand wording and report numeric equivalences. Hypothesis (clarified to match executed analysis): H1 (confirmatory): guarded success rate − baseline success rate ≥ 0.20 (equivalently preregistered regression‑rate reduction ≤ −0.20). Design & tasks: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced 200 stratified intent→golden‑config tasks (small/medium/large topology strata; multi‑vendor features constrained to verifier support). Execution: adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 ran paired episodes (planned 400 episodes) using gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 916b386bd80cbffb...), with shared initial candidate semantics; guarded invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 to validate and allow a single automated repair iteration when violations were detected. Logging & artifacts: all prompts, raw model outputs, verifier traces, parsed IRs, and hashes were archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 8b1a66d7...). Analysis plan: primary inferential test = exact McNemar paired test on complete pairs, plus 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Missingness policy: 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs where both episodes failed) with a prespecified sensitivity analysis treating failed episodes as regressions ('failure-as-regression'), both preregistered and archived.
sections.results: Execution accounting: planned episodes 400; completed 376; failed 24; complete pairs included in primary analysis = 188 (execution_manifest). Primary contingency (complete pairs): n_11=185 (both success), n_10=3 (guarded success only), n_01=0 (baseline success only), n_00=0 (both failure); source: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 522b868e...). Primary estimates (complete‑pair analysis, archived): baseline_success_count = 185/188 (0.9840425531914894), guarded_success_count = 188/188 (1.0); paired success‑rate difference = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25 (artifact: analysis/results.json), 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 reps, seed=1729) for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149]. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥0.20) was not met. Missingness & sensitivity: 12 pairs were excluded from the primary analysis because both episodes failed (missingness_summary.csv: both_missing_pairs=12; failed_baseline_episodes=12; failed_guarded_episodes=12). Prespecified sensitivity (treat failed episodes as regressions): recomputing over all 200 pairs yields baseline_success_count = 185, guarded_success_count = 188, paired difference = 3/200 = 0.015. McNemar discordant counts (n_10=3, n_01=0) are unchanged so exact McNemar p remains 0.25. Repair activity & verifier coverage: provider‑call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) records repair stage invoked in 3 episodes (stage_counts: repair=3). Representative validator traces in the evidence bundle show validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false for many included pairs (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json), indicating that most LLM proposals matched oracle constraints or the verifier reported no violations; this limited the number of opportunities for repairs to alter outcomes. Power & discordant proportion: preregistered power assumed an approximate discordant proportion ≈0.30 (yielding ≈80% power with 200 pairs). Observed discordant proportion among complete pairs = (n_10 + n_01)/188 = 3/188 ≈ 0.016, far below expectation, producing substantially lower power to detect a 20‑pp effect and contributing to the inconclusive p‑value.
sections.discussion: We report a small positive point estimate favoring the guarded pipeline (≈1.6 pp by complete‑pair analysis; 1.5 pp under missingness‑as‑regression sensitivity) that does not meet the preregistered efficacy threshold and is not statistically significant. Two operational factors explain limited observable verifier impact here: (1) ceiling effect—high baseline correctness (~98.4%) leaves little absolute room for improvement; (2) verifier coverage and task selection—the verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) supports a constrained feature set and, for this synthetic task family, most LLM proposals either met oracle constraints or were identical to golden configs, so the verifier rarely triggered repair (repair invocations = 3). The very small number of discordant pairs (3) drives both the point estimate and limited inferential power despite a prespecified paired design. Implications: verifier‑guided pipelines can provide auditability and safety but measurable corrective benefit depends critically on baseline error regimes, verifier coverage relative to model failure modes, and task difficulty. Future work should evaluate settings with higher baseline error (intentional failure injections or harder task families), multiple models, and broader verifier feature coverage to better quantify corrective value and blast‑radius reductions.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic verifier on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor task set, the guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (paired difference ≈0.016; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; exact McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy threshold was not met. Artifact evidence shows few verifier interventions because baseline LLM proposals were already highly correct for this task family. We publish the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts to support follow‑up studies that vary baseline difficulty, verifier scope, and model ensembles.

Orchestration: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed experiments in Dockerized containers; verifier used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: CNSM2026-A1-prereg-v1 preregistration SHA‑256 = feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3 was archived before observing final execution outputs. Initial master prompt reference (immutable archived path): provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Estimand wording correction: the preregistration text used regression‑rate phrasing while the archived analysis executed the paired success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline); these are numerically equivalent (regression_rate_difference = − success_rate_difference). No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini): results do not imply generality across models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4%) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.
